1.text_clean:
1. A ball of mass $(50 \pm 1)$ g is moving with a speed of $(25 \pm 1)$ m s$^{-1}$. What is the fractional uncertainty in the momentum of the ball?
A. 0.02
B. 0.04
C. 0.06
D. 0.08

2.text_clean:
2. The graph shows the variation with time $t$ of the velocity of an object.
[Graph: velocity against t; an inverted parabola starting at 0, rising to a maximum and returning to 0]
What is the variation with time $t$ of the acceleration of the object?
A. [Graph: acceleration against t; straight line decreasing from a positive value through zero to negative]
B. [Graph: acceleration against t; straight line increasing from a negative value through zero to positive]
C. [Graph: acceleration against t; constant positive horizontal line]
D. [Graph: acceleration against t; constant negative horizontal line]

3.text_clean:
3. X and Y are two objects on a frictionless table connected by a string. The mass of X is 2 kg and the mass of Y is 4 kg. The mass of the string is negligible. A constant horizontal force of 12 N acts on Y.
[Diagram: block X (2 kg) connected by a string to block Y (4 kg); 12 N force pulling Y to the right]
What are the acceleration of Y and the magnitude of the tension in the string?
| | Acceleration of Y / m s$^{-2}$ | Tension in the string / N |
A. 2 | 4
B. 2 | 6
C. 3 | 4
D. 3 | 6

4.text_clean:
4. A net force $F$ acts on an object of mass $m$ that is initially at rest. The object moves in a straight line. The variation of $F$ with the distance $s$ is shown.
[Graph: F against s; straight line decreasing from $F_1$ at s = 0 to zero at $s = s_1$]
What is the speed of the object at the distance $s_1$?
A. $\sqrt{\frac{F_1 s_1}{2m}}$
B. $\sqrt{\frac{F_1 s_1}{m}}$
C. $\sqrt{\frac{2F_1 s_1}{m}}$
D. $\sqrt{\frac{4F_1 s_1}{m}}$

5.text_clean:
5. A cyclist rides up a hill of vertical height 100 m in 500 s at a constant speed. The combined mass of the cyclist and the bicycle is 80 kg. The power developed by the cyclist is 200 W. What is the efficiency of the energy transfer in this system?
A. 8 %
B. 20 %
C. 60 %
D. 80 %

6.text_clean:
6. A block rests on a frictionless horizontal surface. An air rifle pellet is fired horizontally into the block and remains embedded in the block.
[Diagram: block on a horizontal surface; dashed path of the pellet entering the block horizontally]
What happens to the total kinetic energy and to the total momentum of the block and pellet system as a result of the collision?
| | Total kinetic energy | Total momentum |
A. no change | no change
B. no change | decreases
C. decreases | no change
D. decreases | decreases

7.text_clean:
7. A ball rolls on the floor towards a wall and rebounds with the same speed and at the same angle to the wall.
[Diagram: top view; ball approaches a vertical wall obliquely and rebounds at the same angle]
What is the direction of the impulse applied to the ball by the wall?
[Diagram: four arrows; A. up (parallel to wall), B. right (towards wall), C. down (parallel to wall), D. left (away from wall)]

8.text_clean:
8. A liquid is vaporized to a gas at a constant temperature.
Three quantities of the substance are the
I. total intermolecular potential energy
II. root mean square speed of the molecules
III. average distance between the molecules.
Which quantities are **greater** for the substance in the gas phase compared to the liquid phase?
A. I and II only
B. I and III only
C. II and III only
D. I, II and III

9.text_clean:
9. An insulated container of negligible mass contains a mass $2M$ of a liquid. A piece of a metal of mass $M$ is dropped into the liquid. The temperature of the liquid increases by 10 °C and the temperature of the metal decreases by 80 °C in the same time.
What is $\frac{\text{specific heat capacity of the liquid}}{\text{specific heat capacity of the metal}}$?
A. 2
B. 4
C. 8
D. 16

10.text_clean:
10. The molar mass of an ideal gas is $M$. A fixed mass $m$ of the gas expands at a constant pressure $p$. The graph shows the variation with temperature $T$ of the gas volume $V$.
[Graph: V against T; a short straight line segment with positive gradient]
What is the gradient of the graph?
A. $\frac{Mp}{mR}$
B. $\frac{MR}{mp}$
C. $\frac{mp}{MR}$
D. $\frac{mR}{Mp}$

11.text_clean:
11. A travelling wave on the surface of a lake has wavelength $\lambda$. Two points along the wave oscillate with the phase difference of $\pi$. What is the smallest possible distance between these two points?
A. $\frac{\lambda}{4}$
B. $\frac{\lambda}{2}$
C. $\lambda$
D. $2\lambda$

12.text_clean:
12. Horizontally polarized light is incident on a pair of polarizers X and Y. The axis of polarization of X makes an angle $\theta$ with the horizontal. The axis of polarization of Y is vertical.
[Diagram: horizontally polarized light passes through polarizer X (axis at angle θ to horizontal) then polarizer Y (vertical axis); transmitted light emerges]
What is $\theta$ so that the intensity of the light transmitted through Y is a maximum?
A. 0°
B. 45°
C. 90°
D. 180°

13.text_clean:
13. The diagram shows an interference pattern observed on a screen in a double-slit experiment with monochromatic light of wavelength 600 nm. The screen is 1.0 m from the slits.
[Photograph: double-slit fringe pattern; a 1.0 cm scale bar spans about ten fringe spacings]
What is the separation of the slits?
A. $6.0 \times 10^{-7}$ m
B. $6.0 \times 10^{-6}$ m
C. $6.0 \times 10^{-5}$ m
D. $6.0 \times 10^{-4}$ m

14.text_clean:
14. A string is fixed at both ends. P and Q are two particles on the string.
[Diagram: string fixed at both ends; P at the midpoint, Q between the midpoint and the right end]
The first harmonic standing wave is formed in the string. What is correct about the motion of P and Q?
A. P is a node and Q is an antinode.
B. P is an antinode and Q is a node.
C. P and Q oscillate with the same amplitude.
D. P and Q oscillate with the same frequency.

15.text_clean:
15. A charge $+Q$ and a charge $-2Q$ are a distance $3x$ apart. Point P is on the line joining the charges, at a distance $x$ from $+Q$.
[Diagram: +Q on the left, P a distance x to its right, −2Q a further 2x to the right]
The magnitude of the electric field produced at P by the charge $+Q$ alone is $E$.
What is the total electric field at P?
A. $\frac{E}{2}$ to the right
B. $\frac{E}{2}$ to the left
C. $\frac{3E}{2}$ to the right
D. $\frac{3E}{2}$ to the left

16.text_clean:
16. Two wires, X and Y, are made of the same material and have equal length. The diameter of X is twice that of Y.
What is $\frac{\text{resistance of X}}{\text{resistance of Y}}$?
A. $\frac{1}{4}$
B. $\frac{1}{2}$
C. 2
D. 4

17.text_clean:
17. A cell has an emf of 3.0 V and an internal resistance of 2.0 Ω. The cell is connected in series with a resistance of 10 Ω.
[Circuit: 3.0 V cell in series with a 10 Ω resistor]
What is the terminal potential difference of the cell?
A. 0.5 V
B. 1.5 V
C. 2.5 V
D. 3.0 V

18.text_clean:
18. Two parallel wires carry equal currents in the same direction out of the paper. Which diagram shows the magnetic field surrounding the wires?
A. [Diagram: field lines circle each wire anticlockwise and enclose both wires in outer loops; zero field between wires]
B. [Diagram: same pattern as A but with clockwise arrows]
C. [Diagram: separate loops around each wire with a straight line between them (downward arrow), loops not enclosing both wires]
D. [Diagram: as C with arrows reversed (upward straight line between wires)]

19.text_clean:
19. A mass at the end of a string is moving in a horizontal circle at constant speed. The string makes an angle $\theta$ to the vertical.
[Diagram: conical pendulum; string at angle θ to the vertical, mass moving in a horizontal circle]
What is the magnitude of the acceleration of the mass?
A. $g$
B. $g\sin\theta$
C. $g\cos\theta$
D. $g\tan\theta$

20.text_clean:
20. A detector measures the count rate from a sample of a radioactive nuclide. The graph shows the variation with time of the count rate.
The nuclide has a half-life of 20 s. The average background count rate is constant.
[Graph: count rate / s$^{-1}$ (8 to 20) against time / s (0 to 25); decreasing curve from 19 at t = 0 to 11 at t = 20 s, about 9.7 at 25 s]
What is the average background count rate?
A. 1 s$^{-1}$
B. 2 s$^{-1}$
C. 3 s$^{-1}$
D. 4 s$^{-1}$

21.text_clean:
21. The mass of a nucleus of iron-56 ($^{56}_{26}$Fe) is $M$.
What is the mass defect of the nucleus of iron-56?
A. $M - 26m_p - 56m_n$
B. $26m_p + 30m_n - M$
C. $M - 26m_p - 56m_n - 26m_e$
D. $26m_p + 30m_n + 26m_e - M$

22.text_clean:
22. The Feynman diagram shows an interaction between a proton and an electron.
[Feynman diagram: p in, n out at one vertex; e$^-$ in, X out at the other vertex; W exchanged between the vertices; time upward]
What is the charge of the exchange particle and what is the lepton number of particle X?
| | Charge of the exchange particle | Lepton number of particle X |
A. $-e$ | $-1$
B. $-e$ | $+1$
C. $+e$ | $-1$
D. $+e$ | $+1$

23.text_clean:
23. The Higgs boson was discovered in the Large Hadron Collider at CERN. Which statements are correct about the discovery of the Higgs boson?
I. It was independent of previous theoretical work.
II. It involved analysing large amounts of experimental data.
III. It was consistent with the standard model of particle physics.
A. I and II only
B. I and III only
C. II and III only
D. I, II and III

24.text_clean:
24. A fuel has mass density $\rho$ and energy density $u$. What mass of the fuel has to be burned to release thermal energy $E$?
A. $\frac{\rho E}{u}$
B. $\frac{uE}{\rho}$
C. $\frac{\rho u}{E}$
D. $\rho u E$

25.text_clean:
25. The diagram shows a simple model of the energy balance in the Earth surface-atmosphere system. The intensities of the radiations are given.
[Diagram: incoming 340 W m$^{-2}$, reflected 100 W m$^{-2}$, outgoing 240 W m$^{-2}$ at top of atmosphere; surface absorption 240 W m$^{-2}$, surface radiation 390 W m$^{-2}$, radiated by atmosphere (to surface) unknown]
What is the average intensity radiated by the atmosphere towards the surface?
A. 100 W m$^{-2}$
B. 150 W m$^{-2}$
C. 240 W m$^{-2}$
D. 390 W m$^{-2}$

26.text_clean:
26. A simple pendulum undergoes simple harmonic motion. The gravitational potential energy of the pendulum is zero at the equilibrium position. How many times during **one** oscillation is the kinetic energy of the pendulum equal to its gravitational potential energy?
A. 1
B. 2
C. 3
D. 4

27.text_clean:
27. When monochromatic light is incident on a single slit a diffraction pattern forms on a screen. The width of the slit is decreased.
What are the changes in the width and in the intensity of the central maximum of the diffraction pattern?
| | Width of the central maximum | Intensity of the central maximum |
A. increases | increases
B. increases | decreases
C. decreases | increases
D. decreases | decreases

28.text_clean:
28. Monochromatic light of wavelength $\lambda$ in air is incident normally on a thin liquid film of refractive index $n$ that is suspended in air. The rays are shown at an angle to the normal for clarity.
[Diagram: air | film | air; incident ray reflected from both surfaces of the film]
What is the minimum thickness of the film so that the reflected light undergoes constructive interference?
A. $\frac{\lambda}{4n}$
B. $\frac{\lambda}{3n}$
C. $\frac{\lambda}{2n}$
D. $\frac{\lambda}{n}$

29.text_clean:
29. A beam of light containing two different wavelengths is incident on a diffraction grating. The wavelengths are just resolved in the third order of diffraction.
What change increases the resolution of the image?
A. Increasing the width of the incident beam
B. Increasing the intensity of light
C. Decreasing the number of lines per unit length in the diffraction grating
D. Decreasing the order of diffraction

30.text_clean:
30. The diagram shows equipotential lines for an electric field. Which arrow represents the acceleration of an electron at point P?
[Diagram: curved equipotential lines labelled 300 V, 200 V, 100 V from left to right; P on the 200 V line; arrows from P: A up (along line), B right, C down (along line), D left]

31.text_clean:
31. Two charged parallel plates have electric potentials of 10 V and 20 V.
[Diagram: upper plate at 20 V, lower plate at 10 V]
A particle with charge +2.0 µC is moved from the 10 V plate to the 20 V plate. What is the change in the electric potential energy of the particle?
A. −20 µJ
B. −10 µJ
C. 10 µJ
D. 20 µJ

32.text_clean:
32. A satellite of mass $m$ orbits a planet of mass $M$ in a circular orbit of radius $r$. What is the work that must be done on the satellite to increase its orbital radius to $2r$?
A. $\frac{GMm}{r}$
B. $\frac{GMm}{2r}$
C. $\frac{GMm}{4r}$
D. $\frac{GMm}{8r}$

33.text_clean:
33. A small magnet is released from rest to drop through a stationary horizontal conducting ring.
[Diagram: bar magnet, N pole down, falling towards a horizontal ring]
What is the variation with time of the emf induced in the ring?
A. [Graph: emf against time; a single positive pulse]
B. [Graph: emf against time; constant positive value switching to constant negative value]
C. [Graph: emf against time; a positive pulse followed immediately by a larger, narrower negative pulse]
D. [Graph: emf against time; small positive pulse, large negative pulse, small positive pulse]

34.text_clean:
34. An alternating supply is connected to a diode bridge rectification circuit.
[Circuit: AC supply connected across a four-diode bridge; load resistor between nodes P and Q]
The conventional current in the load resistor
A. is a maximum twice during one oscillation of the input voltage.
B. is never zero.
C. has a zero average value during one oscillation of the input voltage.
D. can only flow from P to Q.

35.text_clean:
35. The root mean square (rms) current in the primary coil of an ideal transformer is 2.0 A. The rms voltage in the secondary coil is 50 V. The average power transferred from the secondary coil is 20 W.
What is $\frac{N_p}{N_s}$ and what is the average power transferred from the primary coil?
| | $\frac{N_p}{N_s}$ | Average power transferred from the primary coil / W |
A. $\frac{1}{5}$ | 4.0
B. 5 | 20
C. $\frac{1}{5}$ | 20
D. 5 | 100

36.text_clean:
36. Two initially uncharged capacitors X and Y are connected in series to a cell as shown.
[Circuit: cell in series with capacitor X (1.0 µF) and capacitor Y (2.0 µF)]
What is $\frac{\text{voltage across X}}{\text{voltage across Y}}$?
A. $\frac{1}{2}$
B. 1
C. 2
D. 4

37.text_clean:
37. In a photoelectric experiment a stopping voltage $V$ required to prevent photoelectrons from flowing across the photoelectric cell is measured for light of two frequencies $f_1$ and $f_2$. The results obtained are shown.
[Graph: V against f; points $(f_1, V_1)$ and $(f_2, V_2)$ with $V_2 > V_1$]
The ratio $\frac{V_2 - V_1}{f_2 - f_1}$ is an estimate of
A. $e$
B. $h$
C. $\frac{e}{h}$
D. $\frac{h}{e}$

38.text_clean:
38. A beam of electrons moving in the direction shown is incident on a rectangular slit of width $d$.
[Diagram: horizontal electron beam incident on a slit of width d; y direction vertical, parallel to the slit width]
The component of momentum of the electrons in direction $y$ after passing through the slit is $p$. The uncertainty in $p$ is
A. proportional to $d$
B. proportional to $\frac{1}{d}$
C. proportional to $\frac{1}{d^2}$
D. zero

39.text_clean:
39. Some of the nuclear energy levels of oxygen-14 ($^{14}$O) and nitrogen-14 ($^{14}$N) are shown.
[Energy level diagram: $^{14}$O at 4.1 MeV; $^{14}$N excited state at 2.3 MeV and ground state at 0]
A nucleus of $^{14}$O decays into a nucleus of $^{14}$N with the emission of a positron and a gamma ray. What is the maximum energy of the positron and the energy of the gamma ray?
| | Maximum energy of the positron / MeV | Energy of the gamma ray / MeV |
A. 1.8 | 2.3
B. 1.8 | 4.1
C. 2.3 | 1.8
D. 4.1 | 2.3

40.text_clean:
40. The size of a nucleus can be estimated from electron diffraction experiments. What is the order of magnitude of the de Broglie wavelength of the electrons in these experiments?
A. $10^{-15}$ m
B. $10^{-13}$ m
C. $10^{-11}$ m
D. $10^{-9}$ m
